newsitem.title: USA: FBI questioning TWA families about beige bag.
newsitem.headline: FBI questioning TWA families about beige bag.

text.p: FBI agents are asking relatives of TWA Flight 800 crash victims about a beige carry-on bag found in the cabin that has not been linked to any of the passengers aboard the jet, officials said.

The Washington Post reported on Sunday that investigators were also asking about a different item bearing the name "William Kobofovic", a name which so far does not appear to match anyone known to be on the Paris-bound plane.

The Post and other newspapers said FBI agents showed relatives photographs of a soft, beige bag that appeared slightly charred from the explosion that sent the 747 plunging into the ocean off Long Island, New York, on July 17, killing all 230 people aboard.
Joseph Valiquette, spokesman for the FBI in New York, said investigators do not believe the bag contained a bomb, however.

"We are specifically telling these family members that the bag did not contain a bomb. We are merely trying to identify the owner of the bag and determine its placement in the passenger cabin," he said by telephone.
Investigators were still trying to determine whether the TWA crash was caused by mechanical failure, a bomb or a missile.

The Washington Post quoted a number of victim family members as saying FBI agents had also asked them if they knew a person named "William Kobofovic," a name found on a piece of luggage but not on the plane's passenger or crew manifest.
The New York Times said on Sunday the baggage item, which was not further described, was recovered from the ocean crash site but it was not clear if it was actually aboard the plane.
Valiquette said the FBI was not prepared to release more details.
